case_title: Polamuri Chandra Sekhararao @ Chinna @ Babji v. State of A.P.
accused_victim_relationship: Relative (nephew: victim is son of accused's elder sister); prior friction, as the accused was not on good terms with the victim's mother and the victim pursued the accused's daughter
evidence_type: Circumstantial (eyewitnesses PW-1 and PW-2 turned hostile); medical (post-mortem); recovery of knife; forensic (FSL blood on knife); police and technician witness evidence
confession: Oral statement at police station that he had killed the deceased with the knife, as alleged by the prosecution; the Court did not treat it separately as a confession and relied on the surrounding circumstances
aggravating_circumstances: Seventeen injuries, thirteen of them incised cut wounds; killing within the accused's compound; no explanation for the body's presence
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.302 IPC; life imprisonment and fine of Rs. 1,000 (default three months simple imprisonment)
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; conviction and sentence upheld
neutral_facts: On an evening in April 2004, the victim rode a motorcycle to the accused's house, where the accused and two daughters were chatting outside. When the accused asked why the victim had come, the victim reportedly said he wished to marry both of the accused's daughters and challenged the accused to say to whom they would be given. Angered, the accused fetched a long knife from the bedroom and struck the victim several times. The victim collapsed and died there. The accused, accompanied by the two daughters, travelled to a police station on a two-wheeler and handed over the knife to the station writer, stating that the victim had been killed with it. A first information statement was registered on that basis. The victim's body, with multiple bleeding wounds, was found in the compound of the accused's house. The knife was seized in the presence of a steel plant technician. A forensic laboratory found human blood on the knife, though its blood group could not be traced. The post-mortem doctor recorded seventeen injuries, thirteen of them incised cut wounds, and opined death from shock and haemorrhage; the doctor said the wounds could have been caused by a knife like the one recovered. The two daughters had been examined as eyewitnesses but did not support the first information statement when examined in court. The accused had been living apart from the spouse, who lived with her parents together with the daughters, and the victim had been staying in the same house as them. The accused had strained relations with the victim's mother. The accused asserted an alibi of shopping with the daughters, which was not corroborated.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from shock and haemorrhage; seventeen injuries, thirteen of them incised cut wounds
premeditation_planning: Not found; the Court described the killing as provoked by the accused's anger at the victim's conduct
motive: Accepted by the Court: the accused was enraged by the victim's attempt to develop a close relationship with the accused's daughter, which was not to his liking, combined with the accused's poor relations with the victim's mother
key_evidence_accepted: Presence of the body in the accused's compound (admitted); the first information statement Ext P-1 and the accused's presence at the police station; the knife seizure (Ext P-5); the FSL report (Ext P-29); the doctor's evidence on the injuries; the accused's admitted facts
witness_credibility: Hostile daughters' presence at the police station was admitted and the correctness of Ext P-1 was not open to challenge; related witnesses PW-3, PW-4, PW-6 and PW-7 were not discredited merely because of their relationship; the alibi of the hostile witnesses was rejected for lack of support
post_offence_conduct: Went to the police station with the daughters and handed over the knife, stating he had killed the victim (prosecution case); did not explain how the body came to be in his compound
trial_duration: offence: 06.04.2004; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 28.03.2008; Supreme Court: 23.07.2012
legal_representation: Appellant: Chanchal Kumar Ganguli. State/Respondent: Amit K. Nain, D. Mahesh Babu, Mayur R. Shah, Savita Devi
investigation_status: Ext P-1 registered as a s.302 IPC case on 06.04.2004; knife seized under Ext P-5; FSL report obtained; 15 witnesses examined at trial; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.302, life imprisonment. High Court: appeal dismissed, conviction and sentence upheld. Supreme Court: appeal dismissed
prosecution_argument: PW-1 supported Ext P-1 in examination-in-chief and was hostile in cross-examination; the trial court's conclusion rests on other circumstances; motive existed; the accused gave no explanation for the body and the alibi failed
defence_argument: With the hostile eyewitnesses discounted, Ext P-1 cannot be acted upon; PWs-3, 4, 6 and 7 are related to the deceased and their version cannot be relied on; no incriminating circumstance connects the accused
legal_principle_applied: Circumstantial chain analysis; a hostile witness's earlier statement corroborated by admitted presence at the police station; related witnesses not disbelieved merely because of relationship; the accused had to explain the presence of the body in his premises
judicial_aggravating_factors: Brutal knife wounding causing instantaneous death; killing within the accused's compound; no explanation for the body's presence
